title: Convertible credit bundles and per-route fallback rules PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for introducing 'Convertible Credit Bundles' (CCB) and deterministic per-route fallback rules to reduce customer friction at quota boundaries while preserving predictable billing. CCBs allow customers to purchase a single pool of credits that can be consumed by generation tokens, embeddings units, or dedicated throughput bursts according to defined conversion ratios. Per-route fallback rules define deterministic behavior when a request would exceed a route's quota: soft-decline, best-effort degraded response on a lower-cost model, or automatic burst to reserved pool with proportional billing. This PRD defines requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and rollout steps for both features.
background: Customers want simpler buying experiences (one bundle covering multiple usages) and fewer hard failures at quota boundaries. Current plan entitlements are siloed by unit (tokens, embeddings, concurrency) which increases friction and support load. Incidental spikes lead to either hard 429s or emergency billing escalations. The CCB + per-route-fallback approach aims to reduce interruptions, improve perceived reliability, and keep unit economics transparent.
goals: Enable customers to buy convertible bundles with clear conversion ratios (e.g., 1 CCB = 1000 generation tokens OR 50 embed units OR 1 minute of dedicated p99 throughput).
Provide deterministic per-route fallback policies configurable by plan and route (soft-decline, degraded-model fallback, burst-to-reserved, deny).
Ensure billing and metering accurately attribute consumption back to source units and display transparent invoice line items.
Reduce support cases related to unexpected 429/402 quota failures by 30% within first quarter post-launch.
scope_in_scope: API and console UI for purchasing/allocating CCBs and assigning conversion profiles.
Server-side metering logic to map consumed units back to credit pools in real-time.
Per-route fallback engine with policy definitions stored in plan entitlements and evaluated at request time.
Billing export rows and invoice formatting for convertible consumption with rounding rules and reconciliation metadata.
Acceptance criteria, e2e tests, and canary rollout in hosted environment for a subset of customers.
out_of_scope: Full support for converting third-party marketplace credits into CCBs (future work).
Automated AI-driven conversion ratio optimization (requires usage signals and separate experimentation).
On-prem billing integration changes beyond audit logs and local metering compatibility notes.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Conversion ratios will be fixed per-bundle SKU at purchase time to keep invoicing simple; dynamic runtime conversion is deferred.
We will implement 'degraded-model fallback' only for compatible model classes (e.g., same family, lower compute) to avoid quality surprises. Not all routes will be eligible initially.
Soft-decline responses will include structured metadata in headers/body to enable SDKs and console to surface usage warnings to customers.
We favor deterministic, auditable metering over probabilistic heuristics to simplify dispute resolution. This increases implementation complexity but reduces billing noise.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can purchase a CCB SKU from console and see the bundle reflected in their entitlement table within 5 minutes.
API /billing/usage rows show converted consumption with original unit type, conversion factor, and resulting CCB debit for each request in export CSV and internal ledger.

Per-route fallback policy executes deterministically: 1) preferred: complete request billed to CCB, 2) if insufficient: degraded-model fallback applies and both original and fallback consumption recorded, 3) if not eligible: soft-decline returned and logged.
Invoices display CCB consumption with a clear breakdown: original units consumed, conversion factor used, and final charge. Rounding rules documented and consistent with export reconciliation.
SDKs surface a new usage-warning event when a request triggers fallback or soft-decline; at least one official SDK (Python) integrates this event before GA.
At least 3 customers in canary experience a smooth transition with no incidents and reduced support tickets compared to baseline.
E2E tests for metering, billing export, and invoice generation pass in CI for both single-tenant and multi-tenant (hosted) scenarios.
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM handling for billing metadata approved.
success_metrics: 30% fewer quota-related support tickets in the first 90 days after GA
>95% accuracy in CCB-to-unit attribution in billing exports (sampling audit)
At least 80% of eligible over-quota requests are handled by fallback policies instead of hard 429/402 responses for canary customers
Positive NPS comments mentioning simpler billing or fewer interruptions during trial accounts
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: Implement metering MVP, console buy-flow, and CCB ledger. Internal QA and dev-only canary.
Week 3: Enable per-route fallback engine for non-critical routes and internal customers. Begin integration tests with billing export.
Week 4-6: Select 3 low-risk customers for external canary; monitor in dedicated dashboard and freeze changes during evaluation windows.
Week 7: Iterate on conversion ratios and billing wording based on canary feedback. Expand eligibility to more routes and customers.
Week 9: GA for Hosted customers with public docs, SDK updates, and migration playbook for existing plans. Offer opt-in window for Dedicated customers with guidance.
risks: Disputes from customers due to conversion rounding — mitigate with detailed export rows and sample audits.
Unexpected cost exposure if fallback to burst pool is misconfigured — limit initial burst allowances and throttle by default.
Complexity in multi-tenant invoicing when customers combine CCB with committed capacity — require clear guidance and validation rules.
SDK adoption lag could cause poor UX for customers relying on older clients; provide server-side warning headers as fallback.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: CCB consumption rate, per-route fallback frequency, soft-decline rates, invoice-adjustment requests.
Alerts: >5% of requests using fallback for a given customer in 1h window, >0.5% rounding reconciliation exceptions in billing export.
Audit workflow: weekly sampling of random converted rows to validate factors and ledger parity.
docs_and_support: Public PRD (this doc) and a migration playbook for customers moving from siloed entitlements to CCBs.
Admin console help center article detailing conversion math, rounding, and dispute steps.
Support runbook for billing disputes including quick query SQL and sample export rows to attach to tickets.
